title: How to organize the power tool and battery zone | Garage
description:
Holds the powered tools, their packs, and their chargers so a tool is always ready to run and nothing is left charging unattended.

This is the Power Tool and Battery Zone in the Garage. About 60-90 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
One shelf per battery system with its charger mounted at the front edge and no pack sitting on it, every drill and saw in its case or on a labelled hook with guards down, and bits, blades, and sanding discs in the shallow drawer underneath.

THE SIX PASSES
Sort: Line every pack up and run it in the tool it belongs to until you know which ones still hold a charge.
Straighten: Group by battery system rather than by task, so one shelf carries the tools, packs, and charger of a single pl
Shine: Brush or blow the motor vents on each drill and saw clear of packed dust, and clean the battery contacts and t
Safety: Packs come off the charger once they are full and sit at partial charge on a shelf well clear of the fuel can
Standardize: One shelf label per battery system, charger mounted at the front edge, so a pack left charging shows as a lump
Sustain: Pulling a full pack off the charger is part of finishing the job, the same as putting the drill back in its ca

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
No battery sleeps on a charger, and no tool goes back on the shelf with its guard held open.

Full written steps for this zone, free:
https://6s-success.com/zones/garage-the-power-tool-and-battery-zone.html

6S Success turns Lean's six-S method into something you can actually do in a house: Sort, Straighten, Shine, Safety, Standardize, Sustain. One small zone at a time, finished in one session, and it stays finished.
